By the Northeastern Illinois Planning Commission on October 21, 1971, as one of its functional plans (See Exhibit 5).
Lincoln Highway acts as a through route for trucks and passenger vehicles traveling between Indiana and Illinois communities. It also serves the industrial areas to the east of this improvement. It provides access to transportation centers such as the Illinois Central Railroad station at the intersection of Olympian Way and Lincoln Highway. Failure to improve the existing facility will result in the impairment of economic activity as passenger and freight movements through the area will be delayed due to traffic congestion. Likewise, local economic development will progress at a lower rate since access to undeveloped areas will remain poor.
Present automobile and heavy through truck traffic tax the geometric and structural capacities of the existing facility. This section of roadway is classified as obsolete because of deteriorated pavement and structures, drainage problems, traffic congestion and accident experience. Therefore, this facility will no longer meet the present or projected needs of the communities growth, and transportation goals and objectives.
Exhibit "6" is a summary of accidents over a three year period which supports the need for improving the following Lincoln Highway intersections:
1. Governor's Highway and Crawford Avenue
2. Main Street
3. Olympian Way
4. Orchard Drive
5. Western Avenue
6. Hilltop Avenue
7. Division Street
Lincoln Highway is presently the major access route to the western portion of Chicago Heights for three fire stations. Although Stations 1 and 2 are located south of the highway and Station 3 is to the north, the residential street network is such that faster service is obtained by moving directly at the corner of Indiana Street and Lincoln Highway and going west on the major roadway.
Fire protection for the Village of Park Forest does not require the use of Lincoln Highway and the new business district at the corner of Indiana Street and Lincoln Highway will be serviced from Indiana Street.
